context:
Goal: a grant you type in the coordinator reaches the lane it names.
Problem (rule): the plan's planned "self-edit" grant guards nothing, because a lane's file edits in its own checkout never reach auto mode's safety check (measured 12:49 CST). What auto mode actually refuses in a lane is starting an agent, and a new kind of grant needs your word.
Based on (measured): Claude Code 2.1.319: a hook that allows an act skips auto mode's check (9 ms vs 2391 ms).
Based on (ruling): item 221, read as a (12:36 CST): you'll type test lines from the web and phone apps.
Departs from: the plan's list of grants (merge <pr>, self-edit) — becomes one grant: `grant <lane> spawn <n>m`.
On a, task 221 becomes: type `grant grant-reaches-lanes spawn 15m` in the coordinator once from claude.ai on the web and once from the phone app.

options.gain: No retyping grants inside each lane.
options.how: `grant <lane> spawn <n>m` lets every agent start in that lane until the time runs out.
options.label: Build it
options.lose: One grant covers every agent start in that lane for that time.

options.how: Keep typing grants inside each lane.
options.label: Close the plan

short: Grant a lane's spawns from the coordinator
title: Should a grant you type in the coordinator let a named lane start its agents for a set time?
why: It removes the retyping, and the time limit bounds what one grant covers.
